questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an SI base unit?
questions.explanation: The newton is a derived unit (kg m s⁻²); kelvin, ampere and mole are base units.

questions.q: The SI prefix 'micro' stands for a factor of
questions.explanation: Micro means one millionth, 10⁻⁶.

questions.q: What is the dimensional formula of pressure?
questions.explanation: Pressure = force/area = MLT⁻² / L² = ML⁻¹T⁻².

questions.q: In a vernier callipers, 10 vernier divisions coincide with 9 main-scale divisions, and one main-scale division is 1 mm. What is the least count?
questions.explanation: Least count = 1 MSD − 1 VSD = 1 mm − 0.9 mm = 0.1 mm.

questions.q: Which expression for the time period of a mass m attached to a spring of force constant k is dimensionally consistent?
questions.explanation: k has dimensions MT⁻², so m/k has dimensions T² and √(m/k) has dimensions of time.

questions.q: g is found from g = 4π²L/T². The length L is measured with 1% error and the time period T with 2% error. What is the maximum percentage error in g?
questions.explanation: Fractional error = ΔL/L + 2ΔT/T = 1% + 4% = 5%.

questions.q: Convert a density of 1 g cm⁻³ into kg m⁻³.
questions.explanation: Dividing 10⁻³ kg by 10⁻⁶ m³ gives 1000 kg m⁻³.

questions.q: Using dimensional analysis, show that the time period T of a simple pendulum depends on its length l and the acceleration due to gravity g as T ∝ √(l/g). Assume T depends only on l, g and mass m.
questions.answer: Writing T ∝ m^a l^b g^c and equating dimensions gives a = 0, b = ½, c = −½, so T ∝ √(l/g).
keyPoints: Write T = k m^a l^b g^c
Equate dimensions: M: a = 0; L: b + c = 0; T: −2c = 1
So c = −½, b = ½, a = 0, hence T ∝ √(l/g)
questions.explanation: Matching powers of M, L and T on both sides fixes the exponents; the mass drops out.

questions.q: The rate of change of velocity of a body with time is called
questions.explanation: Acceleration a = dv/dt.

questions.q: A body moving with uniform velocity has an acceleration that is
questions.explanation: Uniform velocity means velocity does not change, so acceleration is zero.

questions.q: A particle with initial speed 10 m s⁻¹ moves with a uniform acceleration of 2 m s⁻² over a distance of 24 m. What is its final speed?
A car travels the first half of a journey at 40 km/h and the second half (same distance) at 60 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole journey?
questions.explanation: Average speed = 2v₁v₂/(v₁ + v₂) = 2 × 40 × 60/100 = 48 km/h.

questions.q: Car A moves at a constant 20 m s⁻¹. Car B starts from rest at the same place and the same instant with a constant acceleration of 2 m s⁻² in the same direction. After how long does B overtake A?
questions.explanation: They meet when 20t = ½ × 2 × t², so t = 20 s.

questions.q: A ball thrown vertically upward reaches its highest point. At that instant its acceleration is
questions.explanation: Only the velocity is zero at the top; gravity continues to act, so the acceleration is g directed downward.

questions.q: The position of a particle is x = 3t² + 2t (x in metres, t in seconds). Find its velocity at t = 2 s and its acceleration.
questions.answer: Velocity at t = 2 s is 14 m s⁻¹; acceleration is 6 m s⁻² (constant).
keyPoints: At t = 2 s, v = 14 m s⁻¹
questions.explanation: Differentiate the position once for velocity and twice for acceleration.

questions.q: A stone is thrown vertically upward at 20 m s⁻¹ from the top of a 25 m high building (g = 10 m s⁻²). Find the time it takes to reach the ground and its speed on arrival.
questions.answer: Time = 5 s; speed on arrival = 30 m s⁻¹.
keyPoints: v = 20 − 10 × 5 = −30, so speed 30 m s⁻¹ downward
questions.explanation: Solving the displacement equation with the final position 25 m below the start gives t = 5 s.

questions.q: What is the magnitude of a unit vector?
questions.explanation: A unit vector has magnitude one and only specifies a direction.

questions.q: In uniform circular motion, which of the following remains constant?
questions.explanation: The speed is constant, but the direction of velocity (and hence velocity, momentum and acceleration as vectors) keeps changing.

questions.q: For vectors A = 2î + 3ĵ and B = 4î − ĵ, what is the scalar product A · B?
A projectile is launched at 20 m s⁻¹ at 30° above the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what maximum height does it reach?
If the launch speed of a projectile is doubled while the angle of projection is kept the same, its horizontal range becomes
questions.explanation: Range R = u² sin 2θ / g is proportional to u², so doubling u gives 4 times the range.

questions.q: A boat can move at 5 m s⁻¹ in still water. It is steered perpendicular to the bank of a river flowing at 3 m s⁻¹. What is the boat's speed relative to the ground?
questions.explanation: The two velocities are perpendicular, so v = √(5² + 3²) = √34 ≈ 5.8 m s⁻¹.

questions.q: Resolve a force of 50 N acting at 30° above the horizontal into horizontal and vertical components.
questions.explanation: The components are F cosθ along the horizontal and F sinθ along the vertical.

questions.q: A cyclist rides at a constant speed of 10 m s⁻¹ around a circular track of radius 20 m. Find the centripetal acceleration, the angular speed and the time for one lap.
questions.answer: a = 5 m s⁻²; ω = 0.5 rad s⁻¹; time for one lap = 4π s ≈ 12.6 s.
questions.explanation: Use a = v²/r, ω = v/r and T = 2π/ω.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of linear momentum?
questions.explanation: Momentum = mass × velocity, so its unit is kg m s⁻¹ (equivalent to N s).

questions.q: According to Newton's third law, the action and reaction forces
options: cancel each other on the same body
questions.explanation: They are equal in magnitude, opposite in direction and act on two different bodies, so they cannot cancel each other.

questions.q: A force of 50 N acts on a body for 0.2 s. What is the impulse?
questions.explanation: Impulse = F Δt = 50 × 0.2 = 10 N s.

questions.q: A 0.15 kg ball moving at 20 m s⁻¹ is stopped by a player's hand in 0.1 s. What average force does the hand exert?
Two masses of 3 kg and 5 kg hang from the ends of a light string passing over a smooth light pulley (an Atwood machine). Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is the acceleration of the masses?
A 10 kg block on a rough horizontal floor is pulled by a horizontal force of 30 N. The coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.2 and g = 10 m s⁻². What is the acceleration of the block?
questions.explanation: Friction = 0.2 × 100 = 20 N; net force = 10 N; a = 10/10 = 1 m s⁻².

questions.q: A car of mass 1500 kg must accelerate at 2 m s⁻² against a constant resistive force of 500 N. What forward force must the engine supply through the wheels?
questions.explanation: The driving force must provide the net force and also overcome the resistance.

questions.q: A car rounds a flat circular bend of radius 50 m. The coefficient of friction between the tyres and road is 0.5. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², find the maximum speed with which the car can turn without skidding.
questions.answer: About 15.8 m s⁻¹ (√250 m s⁻¹, about 57 km/h).
keyPoints: Friction provides the centripetal force: μmg = mv²/r
questions.explanation: The maximum friction μmg supplies the centripetal force mv²/r, independent of the car's mass.

questions.q: According to the work–energy theorem, the net work done on a body equals the change in its
questions.explanation: W_net = ΔKE.

questions.q: Which of the following is a conservative force?
questions.explanation: Work done by gravity depends only on the end points, not on the path, so it is conservative.

questions.q: What is the gravitational potential energy of a 5 kg body raised to a height of 4 m? (Take g = 10 m s⁻².)
A machine of power 500 W works for 2 minutes. How much work does it do?
A ball collides head-on elastically with an identical stationary ball. What happens after the collision?
options: The first ball stops and the second moves off with the first one's speed
Both move with half the original speed
The first ball rebounds with the original speed
questions.explanation: For an elastic head-on collision between equal masses, the velocities are exchanged.

questions.q: A 2 kg body moving at 6 m s⁻¹ collides with a 4 kg body at rest and they stick together. How much kinetic energy is lost?
questions.explanation: Common speed = 12/6 = 2 m s⁻¹; KE falls from ½ × 2 × 36 = 36 J to ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 J, a loss of 24 J.

questions.q: How much work does gravity do on a 2 kg ball that falls through 5 m? (g = 10 m s⁻².)
keyPoints: = 100 J (positive, since the force and displacement are in the same direction)
questions.explanation: The work done by gravity is mgh, equal to the gain in kinetic energy.

questions.q: A 2 kg block slides from rest down a smooth incline from a vertical height of 1.8 m (g = 10 m s⁻²). Find its speed at the bottom.
keyPoints: The incline is smooth, so mechanical energy is conserved
questions.explanation: The speed depends only on the vertical drop, not on the angle or the mass.

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: Where is the centre of mass of a uniform thin rod?
options: One-third of the length from one end
One-quarter of the length from one end
questions.explanation: By symmetry, the centre of mass of a uniform rod is at its midpoint.

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: What is the SI unit of angular momentum?
questions.explanation: L = Iω has unit kg m² s⁻¹ (equivalently J s).

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A 1 kg mass is at x = 0 and a 3 kg mass is at x = 4 m on a line. Where is their centre of mass?

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A torque of 20 N m acts on a wheel of moment of inertia 5 kg m². What is its angular acceleration?
questions.explanation: α = τ/I = 20/5 = 4 rad s⁻².

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: The moment of inertia of a uniform rod of mass M and length L about a perpendicular axis through its centre is ML²/12. What is it about a parallel axis through one end?
questions.explanation: Parallel axis theorem: I = ML²/12 + M(L/2)² = ML²/3.

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A solid sphere rolls without slipping on a horizontal surface. What fraction of its total kinetic energy is rotational?
questions.explanation: Rotational KE = ½ × (2/5)mv² = mv²/5; total = 7mv²/10; the fraction is 2/7.

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: Why is it easier to push open a door by applying the force at the edge farthest from the hinges than near the hinges?
questions.answer: The torque is force × perpendicular distance from the hinge; a larger distance gives a larger torque for the same force.
keyPoints: Turning effect is torque τ = r F sinθ
Distance from the hinge (axis) is larger at the edge
So the same force gives a larger torque there
questions.explanation: A bigger lever arm means a smaller force is needed to produce the required torque.

questions.q: The gravitational force between two masses is
options: attractive or repulsive depending on the masses
questions.explanation: Gravitation between any two masses is always attractive.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of the universal gravitational constant G?
questions.explanation: From F = Gm₁m₂/r², G = F r²/(m₁m₂), so its unit is N m² kg⁻².

questions.q: Taking G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², what is the gravitational force between two 1 kg masses 1 m apart?
Taking g = 10 m s⁻² and the radius of the Earth as 6400 km, what is the orbital speed of a satellite revolving just above the Earth's surface?
What minimum work must be done to take a body of mass m from the Earth's surface to infinity (R = radius, g = surface gravity)?
questions.explanation: The surface potential energy is −GMm/R = −mgR, so mgR of work is required.

questions.q: The total mechanical energy of a satellite in a circular orbit around a planet is
options: positive and equal to its kinetic energy
negative and twice its kinetic energy in magnitude
negative and equal in magnitude to its kinetic energy
questions.explanation: KE = GMm/2r and PE = −GMm/r, so total energy = −GMm/2r, equal in magnitude to the KE.

questions.q: What is the acceleration due to gravity at a depth equal to half the Earth's radius below the surface, in terms of the surface value g?
keyPoints: g at depth d is g(1 − d/R)
questions.explanation: Inside a uniform Earth, g decreases linearly with depth.

questions.q: Within the elastic limit, stress is directly proportional to
questions.explanation: This is Hooke's law: stress ∝ strain.

questions.q: Which modulus of elasticity describes the change in volume of a body under uniform pressure?
questions.explanation: Bulk modulus = pressure change / fractional change in volume.

questions.q: A pressure increase of 10⁷ Pa decreases the volume of a liquid by 0.01% (a fractional change of 10⁻⁴). What is its bulk modulus?
questions.explanation: B = ΔP/(ΔV/V) = 10⁷/10⁻⁴ = 10¹¹ Pa.

questions.q: Which of these materials has the largest Young's modulus?
questions.explanation: Steel has Young's modulus of about 2 × 10¹¹ Pa, much larger than lead, rubber or aluminium.

questions.q: The extension of a wire under a load is doubled by increasing the load (within the elastic limit). How does the elastic potential energy stored in the wire change?
questions.explanation: Energy = ½ × (YA/L) × (ΔL)², which is proportional to the square of the extension, so it becomes 4 times.

questions.q: A wire of length L stretches by x under a load F. A second wire of the same material and cross-section, with length L/2, carries the same load. What is its extension?
questions.explanation: Extension ΔL = FL/(AY) is proportional to the length, so the shorter wire stretches by x/2.

questions.q: Distinguish between elastic and plastic behaviour of a material.
questions.answer: A body is elastic if it regains its original shape and size when the deforming force is removed; if the deformation remains after the force is removed (beyond the elastic limit), the behaviour is plastic.
keyPoints: Elastic: complete recovery when force is removed
The elastic limit separates the two
questions.explanation: Beyond the elastic limit a material no longer fully recovers its original dimensions.

questions.q: The upward buoyant force on a body immersed in a fluid equals the weight of the fluid displaced. This statement is known as
questions.explanation: This is Archimedes' principle.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of surface tension?
questions.explanation: Surface tension is force per unit length, so its unit is N m⁻¹.

questions.q: What is the gauge pressure at a depth of 5 m in a liquid of density 800 kg m⁻³? (Take g = 10 m s⁻².)
A body weighs 5 N in air and 3 N when fully immersed in water. What is the buoyant force on it?
questions.explanation: Buoyant force = apparent loss of weight = 5 − 3 = 2 N.

questions.q: Water flows steadily in a horizontal pipe, at 2 m s⁻¹ in the wide part and 6 m s⁻¹ in the narrow part. By how much is the pressure in the wide part higher? (Density of water = 1000 kg m⁻³.)
questions.explanation: Bernoulli: ΔP = ½ρ(v₂² − v₁²) = ½ × 1000 × (36 − 4) = 16000 Pa.

questions.q: The terminal velocity of a small sphere falling through a viscous liquid is proportional to the square of its radius. If the radius is doubled (same material), the terminal velocity becomes
questions.explanation: v_t ∝ r², so doubling r gives 4 times the terminal velocity.

questions.q: Water flows out through a small hole in the side of a tank, 5 m below the free surface. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², find the speed of efflux.
questions.explanation: Applying Bernoulli's principle between the surface and the hole gives v = √(2gh).

questions.q: Explain, using Bernoulli's principle, why the roof of a house may be lifted off during a strong storm.
questions.answer: Fast-moving air over the roof has lower pressure than the still air inside the house, so a net upward force acts on the roof.
keyPoints: Air speed above the roof is high
By Bernoulli's principle, high speed means low pressure
Pressure difference between inside and outside gives a net upward force
questions.explanation: The pressure below the roof is greater than the pressure above it, producing upward lift.

questions.q: Which of the following substances has the highest specific heat capacity?
questions.explanation: Water has a very high specific heat, about 4200 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹.

questions.q: Heat from the Sun reaches the Earth mainly by
questions.explanation: Radiation does not need a material medium, so it can travel through space.

questions.q: A temperature of 300 K corresponds to what Celsius temperature (taking 0 °C = 273 K)?
0.2 kg of water cools from 100 °C to 50 °C. How much heat does it lose? (c = 4200 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹.)
The ends of a metal rod 1 m long and 1 cm² in cross-section are held at 100 °C and 0 °C. Its thermal conductivity is 400 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹. What is the steady rate of heat flow along the rod?
100 g of ice at 0 °C is added to 400 g of water at 20 °C in an insulated container. (Latent heat of fusion of ice = 80 cal g⁻¹; specific heat of water = 1 cal g⁻¹ °C⁻¹.) What is the final state?
options: All the ice melts; mixture at 0 °C
All the ice melts; mixture at 10 °C
questions.explanation: Cooling the water to 0 °C releases 400 × 20 = 8000 cal, which exactly melts 100 g of ice (100 × 80 = 8000 cal).

questions.q: Why does a metal spoon feel colder than a wooden spoon when both are at room temperature?
questions.answer: Metal is a better conductor of heat, so it draws heat from the hand faster than wood, which feels colder.
keyPoints: Both spoons are at the same temperature
Heat leaves the hand faster into the metal
questions.explanation: The sensation of cold depends on the rate of heat loss from the skin, not just on temperature.

questions.q: The zeroth law of thermodynamics leads to the concept of
questions.explanation: If two bodies are each in thermal equilibrium with a third, they are in equilibrium with each other, which defines temperature.

questions.q: In which of the following processes is the work done by the gas zero?
questions.explanation: In an isochoric (constant-volume) process ΔV = 0, so W = PΔV = 0.

questions.q: A refrigerator works between 270 K (inside) and 300 K (outside). What is its maximum coefficient of performance?
questions.explanation: COP = T_cold/(T_hot − T_cold) = 270/30 = 9.

questions.q: A heat engine absorbs 800 J from the source and rejects 600 J to the sink in each cycle. What is its efficiency?
One mole of an ideal gas at 300 K expands isothermally to double its volume. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and ln 2 = 0.693, how much work does it do?
For one mole of an ideal gas, the difference between the molar specific heats at constant pressure and constant volume, Cp − Cv, equals
questions.explanation: Mayer's relation: Cp − Cv = R.

questions.q: State the Kelvin–Planck statement of the second law of thermodynamics.
questions.answer: It is impossible to construct a heat engine that, working in a cycle, takes heat from a single reservoir and converts it entirely into work.
keyPoints: Heat engine operating in a cycle
Heat taken from a single reservoir
Cannot be completely converted into work (efficiency cannot be 100%)
questions.explanation: Some heat must always be rejected to a colder sink.

questions.q: At constant temperature, the pressure of a fixed mass of an ideal gas is inversely proportional to its
questions.explanation: This is Boyle's law: PV = constant at constant temperature.

questions.q: According to Charles's law, at constant pressure the volume of a fixed mass of gas is
options: inversely proportional to its absolute temperature
proportional to the square of its temperature
directly proportional to its absolute temperature
questions.explanation: V/T = constant at constant pressure, with T in kelvin.

questions.q: What is the approximate volume of one mole of an ideal gas at standard temperature and pressure (0 °C, 1 atm)?
questions.explanation: The molar volume of an ideal gas at STP is 22.4 litres.

questions.q: A gas has density 1.2 kg m⁻³ and rms molecular speed 500 m s⁻¹. Using P = ⅓ρv²_rms, what is its pressure?
According to the law of equipartition of energy, what is the total internal energy of one mole of a rigid diatomic ideal gas at temperature T (translation and rotation only)?
questions.explanation: A rigid diatomic molecule has 5 degrees of freedom, each contributing ½RT per mole.

questions.q: Helium (molar mass 4 g/mol) and oxygen (molar mass 32 g/mol) are at the same temperature. What is the ratio of the average translational kinetic energy per molecule of helium to that of oxygen?
questions.explanation: Average translational KE = (3/2)k_BT depends only on temperature, not on the type of gas.

questions.q: Find the average translational kinetic energy of a gas molecule at 27 °C. (Boltzmann constant = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹.)
questions.explanation: Average translational KE per molecule is (3/2)k_BT = 6.21 × 10⁻²¹ J.

questions.q: At the mean position of a particle executing SHM
questions.explanation: At the mean position displacement and acceleration are zero, speed and kinetic energy are maximum.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of angular frequency ω?
questions.explanation: ω = 2π/T, measured in radians per second.

questions.q: A particle's displacement is x = 0.05 sin(20πt) metres. What is the frequency of oscillation?
questions.explanation: ω = 20π rad s⁻¹, so f = ω/2π = 10 Hz.

questions.q: A mass–spring system is taken from the Earth to the Moon. Compared with the time period on Earth, the period on the Moon is
questions.explanation: T = 2π√(m/k) does not depend on g, so it is unchanged.

questions.q: A particle performs SHM of amplitude A and total energy E. What is its kinetic energy when the displacement is A/2?
questions.explanation: PE = E(x/A)² = E/4, so KE = E − E/4 = 3E/4.

questions.q: A mass m is attached to two identical springs, each of force constant k, connected in parallel. Compared with the time period for a single spring, the new period is
questions.explanation: Parallel springs have effective constant 2k, so T = 2π√(m/2k), which is 1/√2 of the single-spring period.

questions.q: The length of a simple pendulum is decreased by 2%. By approximately what percentage does its time period change?
keyPoints: Fractional change in T = ½ × fractional change in l
questions.explanation: Because T depends on the square root of l, the percentage change is halved. A clock with such a pendulum would run fast.

questions.q: In which type of medium is the speed of sound generally the largest?
questions.explanation: Solids are the most rigid, so sound travels fastest in them.

questions.q: When a source of sound moves towards a stationary listener, the apparent frequency heard by the listener
questions.explanation: This is the Doppler effect: an approaching source gives a higher apparent frequency.

questions.q: A sound wave of frequency 170 Hz travels at 340 m s⁻¹. What is its wavelength?
A stationary wave on a string has wavelength 0.6 m. What is the distance between two consecutive nodes?
questions.explanation: Adjacent nodes are separated by λ/2 = 0.3 m.

questions.q: The tension in a stretched string is made four times, with the mass per unit length unchanged. The speed of a transverse wave on the string becomes
questions.explanation: v = √(T/μ), so four times the tension doubles the speed.

questions.q: An open organ pipe is 0.5 m long and the speed of sound is 340 m s⁻¹. What is the fundamental frequency?
questions.explanation: For an open pipe f = v/2L = 340/(2 × 0.5) = 340 Hz.

questions.q: A string has mass per unit length 0.01 kg m⁻¹ and is under a tension of 4 N. Find the speed of a transverse wave on it.
questions.explanation: The wave speed on a stretched string is √(T/μ) = 20 m s⁻¹.
